Here’s How Much a 2024 Lamborghini Urus Performante Costs After 9,000 Miles
14 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
Does the Lamborghini Urus still keep you up at night for whatever reason? Well, we won’t judge you if it does, because it is the Raging Bull’s most popular model ever. On top of that, it’s a family-friendly machine aimed at daily drives, which definitely goes like stink.
The family comprises a single member at the moment. It is the Urus SE Performante unveiled earlier this year, and while it may be an extremely important model for the brand, it does not get that much attention. It has 801 hp (812 ps/597 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque in total from its 4-liter twin-turbo plug-in hybrid V8, and this makes it 12 hp (12 ps/9 kW) more powerful than the Urus SE. It is also 144 hp (146 ps/107 kW) punchier than the S and Performante versions of the exotic crossover.
Lamborghini’s new Urus SE Performante , which will keep the Urus on the appealing side of the segment for as long as possible, as a successor is nowhere in sight just yet, takes only 3.3 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill. And while that may be an 0.1-second improvement over the Urus SE, it cannot beat the Performante. But it does something the latter cannot do, as it does not benefit from an electrified powertrain, namely travel for 37 miles (60 km) or so on electric power alone.
Some say that the Lamborghini Urus Performante remains the sweet spot of the series, even if it is dead and buried, and if you believe the same, then you may want to keep reading, because the example pictured in the gallery above is searching for a new home in the United States of America as we speak. As mentioned in the title, it is a 2024 model year car, and has in the region of 9,000 miles (~14,500 km) on the clock. Therefore, it is a low-mileage example, and it definitely looks very good both inside and out.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago This Lamborghini Urus Performante features a purple paint finish on the outside with a satin look, has plenty of black details for contrast, and rides on a set of bi-tone alloys that combine silver and copper. Shod in sticky tires from Pirelli and decorated with the Raging Bull’s emblem in the middle, the alloys spin around the black brake calipers, which feature Lamborghini branding on them in white. This machine also features tinted windows, though the interior has opened up to the camera.
Step inside and you will see plenty of Alcantara upholstery in black, joined by black leather and some white leather strips for a bit of contrast here and there. The vehicle also features white stitching for more contrast, has the Urus name embroidered into the seatbacks, the Raging Bull’s logo on the integrated headrests, and the Performante emblem on the outer bolsters. The dashboard panel was wrapped in Alcantara, and there is plenty of carbon fiber trim on deck, as well as a red 12 o’clock marker on the steering wheel.
For what it’s worth, it seems that there isn’t anything wrong with this particular Lamborghini Urus Performante , as it looks pretty much like it just left the showroom floor. The vendor hasn’t mentioned any known flaws, but then again, it did not have much to say about it, and it chose to keep the powertrain details away from the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago However, we will remind you that this model, as well as the Urus S, which is also dead and buried, have 657 horsepower (490 kW/666 ps) available via the right pedal, and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque. According to the spec sheet, the Urus Performante needs just 3.3 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, and this makes it two-tenths of a second faster than the S, which uses the same 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 engine in the same configuration. Flat-out, it will do 190 mph (306 kph), whereas the S will top out at 189 mph (305 kph).
In today’s used car market, the Lamborghini Urus Performante usually costs from $250,000 to over $320,000 in the United States of America, though a later model year with only a few miles under its belt in pristine condition can change hands for almost $400,000. So, how much do you think the pictured 2024 model year crossover with its 9,000 miles or so is worth? Unless you said $329,995, then you are wrong, because this was the asking price at the time of writing.
The vehicle is advertised by @motorcarsofchicago on social media. The vendor accepts trade-ins, offers financing, and you know what to do if you want this machine, don’t you? But realistically speaking, is this Lamborghini Urus Performante worth $330K in your opinion? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Motor Cars of Chicago (@motorcarsofchicago)
